scheme: SBI Large Cap Fund (formerly SBI Bluechip Fund)
text: SBI Large Cap Fund (formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund) is an open-ended equity scheme predominantly investing in large cap stocks, with 80-100% allocation to large-cap equities and the remainder across other equities, REIT/InvIT units, debt and money-market instruments per the SID. The scheme's stated benchmark is the BSE 100 TRI.

facts.asset_allocation: 80-100% large-cap equities; up to 20% other equities; up to 10% REIT/InvIT units; up to 20% debt and money-market instruments
facts.as_of: Per scheme detail page on sbimf.com (accessed May 2026)

scheme: SBI Large Cap Fund (formerly SBI Bluechip Fund)
text: The Scheme Information Document (SID) for SBI Large Cap Fund (formerly SBI Bluechip Fund) is the authoritative source for asset allocation, expense ratio, exit load, minimum investment amounts, and benchmark for the scheme. Always read the latest SID for current figures rather than third-party summaries.

scheme: SBI Large Cap Fund (formerly SBI Bluechip Fund)
text: The Key Information Memorandum (KIM) for SBI Bluechip / SBI Large Cap Fund summarises minimum application amount, minimum SIP, plans/options, riskometer, and load structure. The latest KIM on sbimf.com supersedes earlier copies.

SBI Flexicap Fund is an open-ended dynamic equity scheme that invests across large cap, mid cap and small cap stocks; its benchmark is the BSE 500 Index TRI. Refer to the scheme page on sbimf.com and its latest SID for asset-allocation bands, expense ratio, exit load and minimum investment.

facts.category: Flexi Cap Fund (open-ended dynamic equity scheme)
facts.asset_allocation: Diversified across large cap, mid cap and small cap equities, plus debt and money-market instruments per the SID
facts.as_of: Per scheme detail page on sbimf.com (accessed May 2026)

text: The Scheme Information Document (SID) for SBI Flexicap Fund is the authoritative source for asset allocation, fees, exit load and minimum investment for the scheme. Use the latest SID on sbimf.com when answering scheme-specific factual questions.

scheme: SBI ELSS Tax Saver Fund (formerly SBI Long Term Equity Fund)
text: SBI ELSS Tax Saver Fund (formerly SBI Long Term Equity Fund) is an open-ended Equity Linked Savings Scheme with a statutory 3-year lock-in; investments up to Rs 1,50,000 per financial year qualify for deduction under Section 80C of the Income-tax Act, 1961, subject to applicable law. The scheme's benchmark is the BSE 500 TRI; per the latest scheme materials, minimum investment / SIP starts at Rs 500 and exit load is NIL given the statutory lock-in.

facts.notes: Lock-in is statutory for ELSS; tax deduction is per current Section 80C limits and applicable law.
facts.as_of: Per scheme detail page on sbimf.com (accessed May 2026)

scheme: SBI ELSS Tax Saver Fund (formerly SBI Long Term Equity Fund)
text: The factsheet for SBI ELSS Tax Saver Fund publishes monthly disclosures including portfolio holdings, expense ratio, riskometer, benchmark and statistical ratios. For current numbers always open the latest factsheet on sbimf.com.

scheme: SBI ELSS Tax Saver Fund (formerly SBI Long Term Equity Fund)
text: The SID for SBI ELSS Tax Saver Fund describes the 3-year statutory lock-in, Section 80C eligibility within prescribed limits, asset-allocation bands, fees and exit load. Tax treatment depends on current law and individual circumstances.

SBI Mutual Fund publishes a scheme differentiation document for its equity schemes summarising category, investment objective, asset-allocation bands and benchmark side-by-side. Use it for quick scheme-vs-scheme factual comparisons before opening individual SIDs.

SBI Mutual Fund maintains a public FAQ covering common investor questions on transactions, KYC, statements, redemption, switches, taxation and online services. For specific procedural steps, consult the FAQ on sbimf.com.

SBI Mutual Fund offers Smart Statement and account/capital-gains statement downloads via the investor portal; investors can request statements by entering their PAN and registered email or by logging in to the online transaction portal. Use the official Smart Statement page on sbimf.com for the latest steps.

SBI Mutual Fund's SIP page describes how Systematic Investment Plans work, eligible frequencies and how to start a SIP online. Minimum SIP amounts are scheme-specific and stated in each scheme's KIM/SID.

SBI Mutual Fund's Equity Mutual Funds page lists open equity schemes across SEBI categories such as large-cap, flexi-cap, mid-cap, small-cap, ELSS and others. Use this listing to navigate to a specific scheme's detail page.

SBI Mutual Fund's official site is the entry point to scheme pages, NAV, factsheets, KIM/SID, statements and investor services. For any scheme, use the latest KIM, SID and factsheet for authoritative figures.

Per SEBI categorisation, large-cap stocks are the top 100 listed companies by full market capitalisation, mid-cap stocks rank 101-250, and small-cap stocks rank 251 and beyond; AMFI updates the master list every six months. ELSS schemes invest predominantly in equities and have a statutory lock-in under Section 80C.

facts.large_cap_definition: Top 100 listed companies by full market capitalisation
facts.mid_cap_definition: 101st to 250th company by full market capitalisation
facts.small_cap_definition: 251st company onwards by full market capitalisation
facts.notes: Source circular: SEBI/HO/IMD/DF3/CIR/P/2017/114 (6 Oct 2017); AMFI publishes the master list every six months.

text: The Riskometer is a SEBI-mandated standardised risk disclosure for mutual fund schemes, updated on an ongoing basis as per SEBI's Master Circular on Mutual Funds. Each AMC publishes monthly riskometer disclosures for its schemes; for any specific scheme refer to its latest factsheet.

AMFI's investor education page on risks in mutual funds explains common categories such as market risk, credit risk, liquidity risk and concentration risk, and notes that NAV fluctuations depend on movements in security prices. Mutual fund investments are subject to market risks; read all scheme-related documents carefully.

AMFI's 'What are Mutual Funds' page is the standard introduction covering pooled investment vehicles, professional management, units, NAV, types of schemes and how investors transact. It is the recommended starting point for general MF education.
AMFI hosts NAV history and downloads for mutual fund schemes; NAV is the per-unit value at which investors transact and is published daily as per regulatory requirements.

The Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) is the industry body for Indian mutual funds and publishes investor-oriented information, NAV data, riskometer pointers and circulars on its official website.

SEBI's Investment Management Department (IMD) is responsible for the regulation, registration and supervision of mutual funds, portfolio managers and collective investment schemes in India. Mutual fund regulations and circulars issued by SEBI are published on sebi.gov.in.

SEBI's investor portal hosts an 'Understanding Mutual Funds' module with foundational concepts: pooled investments, AMCs, fund managers, NAV, types of schemes (open-ended, closed-ended, interval), and active vs passive styles. Use it for neutral, regulator-published education.
